examples.knowledge_point: Finding Two Scalar Factors in a Linear Combination
examples.problem:
Consider the picture below. Given that $\mathbf{m}=\lambda\mathbf{n}+\mu\mathbf{k}$, find $\lambda$ and $\mu$.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14073957/assets/b8abf22d14f93a38c4d01f368b8171e4ccfe90086d932f5b58453baa46391405.png)
examples.worked_solution:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14073957/assets/76b9867a7c1ef484922241ebe44272f0104e406c31310bf36227a13850f50d8b.png)

In $\bigtriangleup ONM$ shown above, we have:

- $ON=2|\mathbf{n}|$;

- $\overrightarrow{ON}$ and $\mathbf{n}$ have the same direction

Hence, $\overrightarrow{ON}=2\mathbf{n}$.

Similarly:

- $NM=2|\mathbf{k}|$

- $\overrightarrow{NM}$ and $\mathbf{k}$ have the same direction

Hence, $\overrightarrow{NM}=2\mathbf{k}$.

Additionally, 

$$
\begin{aligned}m & =\overset{\to }{ON}+\overset{\to }{NM} \\  & =2n+2k.\end{aligned}
$$

Consequently, $\mathbf{m}=\lambda\mathbf{n}+\mu\mathbf{k}=2\mathbf{n}+2\mathbf{k}$. 

Since $\mathbf{n} \nparallel \mathbf{k},$ the linear combination can only be written in one way. Equating the coefficients of $\mathbf{n}$ and $\mathbf{k}$, we get:

- $\lambda=2$ and $\mu=2$

feedback.worked_solution:
To find $\lambda ,$ we want to match the expression

$$
c=\lambda a-2b.
$$

We are given that one of the components is $-2b.$ So, we first draw the vector $-2b$ from the origin. Then we complete the path to the point $C.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14073957/assets/7e6923e8b8b774eeaa2f885ec6aa24bb03f07c547fa50e7145a4113a18e92e8a.png)

Let $P$ be the endpoint of the vector $-2b.$ Then

$$
c=\overset{\to }{OP}+\overset{\to }{PC}.
$$

In $△OPC,$ we have:

- $PC=2|a|$

- $\overset{\to }{PC}$ and $a$ have opposite directions

Hence, $\overset{\to }{PC}=-2a.$

Additionally,

$$
\begin{aligned}c & =\overset{\to }{OP}+\overset{\to }{PC} \\  & =-2b-2a.\end{aligned}
$$

Consequently, $c=\lambda a-2b=-2a-2b.$

Since $a∦b,$ the linear combination can only be written in one way. Equating the coefficients of $a,$ we get:

$$
\lambda =-2
$$
